#4077. Xenogears Is Finally Getting Remastered, But Not in the Way You Think

Murillo Zerbinatto is a JRPG enthusiast, writer, and editor. He has played over 300 RPGs during his gaming career, with 90% of them being JRPGs.

There are two perspectives on remasters and remakes. On one hand, we have those who complain whenever a developer announces a new one, wishing they would dedicate development efforts to bringing new IPs to life. On the other hand, we have those who rejoice and feel the nostalgia tingling whenever a game that shaped their tastes returns to the modern era. I fall into the latter camp, which is why I am extremely excited for the upcoming fanmade remaster of Xenogears.

The Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey, the long-forgotten Nokia N-Gage RPG, is returning!

To be fair, three Xenogears remasters are currently being developed by fans, each with its own codename: Weltall, Exodus, and Atlas. Today I'll discuss the Atlas remaster because it seems to be the one the fanbase is most excited about, and it already has an imminent release date of 15 December 2026. However, keep in mind that since this is not an official remaster from Square Enix, you can only legally play it if you own an original copy of Xenogears at home.

The project could hardly be called a Xenogears remaster if it didn't include notable upgrades over the original. According to the creator, Reddit user Ok-Bed3203, the entire game has been rebuilt in the Godot engine and will run directly inside it, provided you supply your own copy of the game. Fans can experience Xenogears Atlas in two distinct visual styles, dubbed Canon and HD.

In Canon mode, the visuals remain faithful to the 1998 release, while incorporating technical fixes such as eliminating flickering triangles or textures, stabilizing sprites and images, and smoothing out screen fades. Meanwhile, High Definition mode introduces enhanced textures and sprites, 16:9 widescreen support (with menus, text, and FMVs preserved in their original 4:3 framing so nothing gets stretched), updated lighting and visual effects, and 3D Gears.

Both modes will support 60 FPS, 120 FPS, or your monitor's native refresh rate. They also include 2K CG cutscenes upscaled by Laichzeit (likely exclusive to HD mode, though not explicitly specified), subtitles in every language, fan translations, and quality-of-life options like text speed adjustments, quick loads, full-screen or windowed modes, and automatic pausing when running in the background.

Independent developer LoreanXavier, also known as Lorean The Gamer, has been working on an unofficial native PC port of P.T. for quite some time.

After the initial release, the developers plan to add a Mods menu that lets you load custom text patches and swap images or audio files by name, along with remastered music from Xenogears' iconic soundtrack and further touch-ups to the 2K movies. The community has also suggested several additions currently under consideration, including random encounter rate toggles, a reduced-flash mode, auto-advancing dialogue, optional voice-over via the Spoken Mirror fan dub (slated to arrive alongside the Disc 2 remake), and a dedicated Android port.

As you probably noticed, the developer mentioned a Disc 2 remake. That sounds like a tall order, because as anyone who played the game remembers, Xenogears features a pristine Disc 1, whereas the second disc was famously rushed after Square cut the budget before the project could be finished, which severely undermined the experience. Atlas aims to give Disc 2 the breathing room it never received. While it is not yet completely clear what that will entail or when it will arrive, it is easily the most intriguing prospect of this entire fanmade remaster.

While the project looks incredible and has me thoroughly hyped, one looming question always hangs in the air these days: was this project made using AI? The developer preemptively addressed that very concern:

“About AI, since it always comes up: yes, I used AI as a tool along the way, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. But this is not a vibe-coded project. I checked every cutscene, every movement and every 16:9 margin by hand, then fixed it and compared it with the original. A huge part of the work was the boring part: tracking down the smallest glitches left over from the PS1 renderer, one by one, until they were gone. Monk work, honestly. I hope you'll feel it when you play.”

About AI, since it always comes up: yes, I used AI as a tool along the way, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

So there you have it. If you want to experience or revisit Xenogears with revamped visuals, quality-of-life additions, tweaks, and technical fixes, Xenogears Atlas might just be the way to go. This Xenogears remaster launches on 15 December 2026, via Godot for PC, though you will still need your original copy to get it running. Who knows, maybe this will finally wake Square Enix up to greenlight a full-fledged official remaster, or at least sell the IP back to Tetsuya Takahashi.

#4075. Random: GTA 6 Hides An Adorable Mario & Luigi Easter Egg In Its Massive World

After 13 long years, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out and breaking records left, right, and centre. While folks who only own a Switch or Switch 2 can't get in on the action, we can at least appreciate a good Easter Egg when we see one.

Case in point, the game contains a pretty blatant nod to Mario and Luigi if you know where to look. As highlighted by TheGamingRevolution on YouTube, heading to Lummox County in the north of Leonida and locating a ruined site in the countryside will yield a pair of hats that look remarkably similar to the attire made famous by Nintendo's brotherly mascots.

Essentially, at the top of the ruins, you'll notice a near-invisible block floating just above the main structure. Reaching the top and then jumping into the block will cause it to burst, revealing two hats: one is red with the letter 'J' adorned for Jason, and the other green with the letter 'L' for Lucia.

It's a lovely little nod to Nintendo, and one that we suspect most people will never see. @Lizuka The recent Xbox "glitch" has shown that the game isn't as CPU-intensive as initially thought. It basically unlocks the game's frame rate, but keeps the game logic to 30fps, so while an Xbox Series X could be running it at 45-50fps, everything is faster like it's sped up at ~1.5x.

The Series S using this glitch has a minor improvement, though looking upwards allows it to increase the frame rate because it's not having to render as much. So in this particular case, the GPU is the bottleneck. The game forces a 720p native render before upscaling to 1080p, and there is no dynamic resolution scaling to lessen the load. The idea was that a Witcher 3 solution could be used by shifting CPU tasks to the GPU. With seeing the CPU utilization not being as heavy as once thought, it makes it that much more valid to use this trick, especially on simulations that don't need immediately reactions.

A hypothetical Switch 2 version would not need to render at 720p. They could render as low as 540p if needed (docked), reducing GPU and RAM bandwidth utilization, and then upscale to 1080p with DLSS. Use of dedicated RT cores will help as well because they are not only more complete, but can run concurrently with rendering. Series S uses RDNA 2, which digs into the GPU shader and TMU resources, cutting into the render budget because it can't be don concurrently.

Honestly, Series S tends to get the lazy treatment from developers, but Rockstar is not one of those. If they are willing to put in the time to craft a Series S version to look as good as it does, then they should be capable of making a good Switch 2 version.

#4074. GTA 6 Interactive Map - Every Location in Leonida

Leonida covers six regions, from the beaches and islands of Vice City to the forests of Mount Kalaga, and it is packed with places worth knowing about. Safehouses, banks worth robbing, the nearest Ammu-Nation and the closest Pay 'n' Spray are all out there, if you know where to look.

The interactive map below fixes that. It puts 1,075 places across all of Leonida on one map you can search, filter and tick off as you go, from robbery targets to hidden packages. Here is how to use it and what you will find.

The map works like any online map: drag to move and zoom in on the part of Leonida you care about. Every marker belongs to a category, and the sidebar is where you choose what to see.

The map sorts its 1,075 places into nine categories, listed here in the same order as the sidebar. Food & Drink is by far the busiest, so switch it off first if a district looks crowded.

Banks (25), Illegal Operations (43), Smash 'n' Grabs (36), Payday Loans (7), Fences (13)

Gyms (9), Golf Courses (3), Gang Compounds (2), Random Events (5)

Gas Stations (62), Pay 'n' Sprays (19), Mod Shops (16), Car Washes (7), Vehicle Dealers (2), Public Transport (44)

Clothing (70), Footwear (17), Hair & Beauty (19), Tattoos (11), Electronics (15)

Street Food (151), Bars (138), Cafes & Takeout (104), Convenience Stores (75), Fast Food (33), Liquor Stores (14)

Landmarks (41), Cities & Towns (10), Marinas (11), Nightclubs (6), Police Stations (5), Fire Stations (4), Hospitals (3), Cinemas (1)

Some markers may sit slightly off their actual locations, and new places are added as players find them. For more on Leonida's regions, characters and activities, head to the Fextralife GTA 6 Wiki, which features the same map on its Interactive Map page.

#4073. Arc Raiders finally reveals early 2026 roadmap, but we’re not getting a new map for a while

The first couple of months of 2026 in the world of Arc Raiders look pretty promising, but the big guns are being held back for now.

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

#4071. 10 Fighting Games That Totally Reinvent Themselves Halfway Through

Manuel Sifontes is a content strategist and multimedia journalist specializing in technology, culture, and storytelling. He crafts clear, engaging narratives and builds digital audience growth.

I am a full-time fighting game enthusiast. I thrive on those intense, white-knuckle matches that push my skills to the limit—even when I have to retry a tough fight over and over. Honestly, half the magic lies in that process of adapting until you finally break through the wall. Beyond pure mechanics, though, I have a special soft spot for titles that refuse to stay boxed in, introducing new rules and systems as you progress until they practically reinvent themselves halfway through.

Having played countless fighting games over the years, a handful stand out for how dramatically they shift their rules, mechanics, or entire structure mid-match, mid-mode, or halfway through a campaign. They genuinely caught me off guard when I first played them, keeping the experience fresh instead of letting it settle into a predictable loop. Here are 10 fighting games that pull off that kind of reinvention, ranked from the cleverest twists to the most radical genre-bending shifts.

I grew up alongside Goku and his friends, sinking hundreds of hours into every Dragon Ball game on the PlayStation 2 and PS4. Naturally, I nearly teared up with excitement when Dragon Ball: Sparking! ZERO was announced—and once I finally got my hands on it, the combat immediately won me over, recapturing the spirit of Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 with sharper visuals and an expanded roster.

As I dove deeper into its Episode Battle campaign, however, I realized it wasn't just retreading familiar manga and anime arcs. By fulfilling specific hidden objectives mid-fight—like defeating an opponent within a strict time limit or making an unexpected choice—you unlock Sparking! Episodes, which act as full-fledged "What If?" timelines that rewrite the rest of that character's campaign. Seeing the story branch off into uncharted territory made clearing the main mode feel far more exciting than simply replaying the same plot beats we all know by heart.

I have been a die-hard fan of Jin Kazama's saga ever since I first booted up Tekken 3 on the original PlayStation, and I've played nearly every entry since—including Tekken 7 on PS4 (following its 2015 arcade debut). Beyond bringing an expanded roster and memorable newcomers to the table, it also shook up the formula halfway through its main story campaign to give the climax far more dramatic weight.

Throughout the first half of The Mishima Saga, the game sticks to the series' classic blueprint: straightforward one-on-one bouts fought under standard Tekken rules. Once Heihachi reclaims the Mishima Zaibatsu in the second half, though, the campaign throws traditional tournament rules out the window in favor of boss encounters featuring super armor phases, special EX and Rage meters, health regeneration, and mid-fight Quick-Time Events that turn battles into cinematic spectacles. Those mechanics completely changed how I approached the late-game fights, forcing me to play much more defensively so I wouldn't enter the next phase with a depleted health bar.

Mortal Kombat is another legendary franchise that has delivered decades of over-the-top violence, though narrative fatigue and identity issues eventually pushed NetherRealm Studios to hit the reset button with Mortal Kombat 1.

I placed Mortal Kombat 1 here because of how dramatically it flips both its narrative tone and its opponent design in the final stretch of its Story Mode. Across the first 14 chapters, the campaign presents a relatively grounded reboot centered on martial arts tournaments and political intrigue within Liu Kang's New Era.

Once the story reaches its climax at the Pyramid of Argus, however, the multiverse blows wide open and pits you against procedurally generated hybrid fighters that mash up the appearances, special moves, and Fatalities of two different characters into one. Facing off against unpredictable fusions completely changes how you read opponents on the fly, turning the finale into a chaotic, anything-goes brawl.

The best fighting games with worthwhile campaigns have unique mechanics and interesting stories.

Another absolute favorite from my old PS2 days—and one I would love to see get a proper remake or sequel—is Def Jam: Fight for NY. It let you build your own custom brawler and drop straight into a gritty turf war packed with betrayals, brutal environmental knockouts, and some of the biggest hip-hop icons of the era.

What really hooked me in its Story Mode was how your moveset evolves halfway through the climb. You start by creating your fighter and picking a single base discipline from five options: Martial Arts, Wrestling, Submissions, Kickboxing, or Streetfighting. Later on, by training at Stapleton Athletics gym, you unlock the ability to buy and fuse up to three distinct fighting styles onto your character—completely rewriting your combo strings, counters, and Blazin' finishers depending on the exact styles you combine.

You can't talk about standout modern fighting games without bringing up Street Fighter 6, a title I have easily poured dozens of hours into. Much like the other entries on this list, its single-player journey gradually reinvents itself into something far wilder than its opening hours suggest.

Early on in World Tour, you control a rookie avatar roaming Metro City with a bare-bones moveset while learning the fundamentals of the Drive System. Once you travel to Nayshall and start training under multiple Masters from the main roster, however, the mode opens up into a full-blown hybrid moveset sandbox. Before long, you can mix and match special moves from completely incompatible archetypes—pairing Ryu's Hadoken with Zangief's Spinning Piledriver and Chun-Li's kicks—exclusively within World Tour and the Battle Hub.

These ten fighting games are the best to come back to and fight through solo or against friends time and time again.

Unlike most games on this list, Nidhogg reinvents its genre dynamically in the middle of every single match. Each bout begins in the center of the stage as a tense, minimalist one-on-one fencing duel where spacing, blade height, and timely disarms mean everything.

The moment one player scores a kill, though, the game instantly mutates from a methodical duel into a frantic obstacle-course platformer. The winner has to sprint across multiple screens toward their goal while the defeated player repeatedly respawns ahead to stop them using any dirty trick available—from dive kicks to throwing their sword—flipping attacker and defender roles back and forth until someone finally reaches the end to be devoured by the giant Nidhogg worm.

As we climb closer to the top spot, the mid-game transformations become much more drastic. At its core, For Honor is built around its Art of Battle directional guard system, demanding careful reads in close-quarters melee duels—and in its large-scale Breach mode, the first two phases revolve around escorting or halting a battering ram.

Introduced with the Marching Fire expansion in October 2018, Breach completely changes its structure once the ram breaks through both gates. At that point, the ram disappears and the match transforms into an asymmetrical raid with limited respawn tickets, forcing the attacking team to coordinate and take down an AI-controlled Commander with massive health and area-of-effect attacks while defenders fight to keep him alive—turning tactical skirmishes into a high-stakes team raid.

Originally released in arcades in 1996 before finally reaching modern consoles and PC in 2022 via Capcom Fighting Collection, although it's one of those games from the Japanese company that desperately needs a remake. Red Earth (known as Warzard in Japan) took a wildly unconventional approach to the genre. Rather than pitting you against a traditional lineup of rival fighters, it built its main Quest Mode around full-fledged RPG progression.

It kicks off like a classic Capcom 2D fighter with a striking dark-fantasy aesthetic, letting you choose from four heroes, before quickly shifting into a boss-rush RPG. As you clear battles, your character earns experience, levels up, unlocks new special moves, and picks up elemental orbs and weapons off the ground to survive multi-phase encounters against towering monsters that mutate and change their attack patterns mid-fight.

Video game studios have done a great job of bringing retro fighting games to modern platforms, but a few are still trapped on antiquated systems.

Super Smash Bros. Brawl remains a beloved favorite for many fans, and its main campaign pulled off a full-blown genre switch in its second act. Throughout the first half of The Subspace Emissary, the mode plays like a linear, side-scrolling beat 'em up broken into distinct stages with rotating pairs of heroes—a straightforward formula I genuinely enjoyed.

However, once the roster finally unites in Subspace and suffers a crushing defeat at the hands of Tabuu, the entire mode transforms into The Great Maze. Suddenly, those linear stages give way to a massive, interconnected, non-linear Metroidvania-style map where you command the entire unlocked roster, rescue captured trophies, and backtrack through merged zones to rematch bosses—a sudden shift in structure that completely caught me off guard back in the day.

When it comes to fighting games that radically reinvent themselves halfway through, Soulcalibur III takes the crown. On the surface, it serves as the direct follow-up to Soulcalibur II's fast-paced, 3D weapon-based combat built around smooth 8-Way Run movement—familiar territory for anyone who loved the series on PlayStation 2.

Inside its signature Chronicles of the Sword campaign, however, the game fuses traditional one-on-one weapon duels with a real-time strategy game. You command squads across a tactical map, capture strongholds, and level up custom-built units—and by the second half of the campaign, early small-scale skirmishes escalate into complex, multi-front sieges against iconic series veterans and high-level bosses that test both your strategic planning and your blade skills.

Looking for a quick brawl? These games have got you covered.

#4070. Nioh 3’s generous demo is out now, and your progress carries over to the full game

If you’re looking for a way to check out one of the biggest releases of early 2026, Team Ninja has made it easy for you.

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

#4069. The Video Games You Should Play This Weekend – November 20, 2026

This is it. We finally made it. Grand Theft Auto VI is here. I have played the game for a number of hours and read Matt Miller's glowing review, which you can read here, and I still don't know if I personally believe the game is actually out. But that just might the lack of sleep from staying up late to play Grand Theft Auto VI.

Many games chose to avoid the blast radius of Rockstar's latest crime caper, but that doesn't mean it's the only game that came out this week and you can find them below. But as is tradition, here are some of our top stories of the week first.

If you’re not aware that GTAVI launched this week, it’s possible that you’ve been living under a rock somewhere. Nonetheless, we’re here to offer the reminder that after more than a decade of waiting for a new installment, Rockstar has this week rolled out its new game. It’s good. Like, really good, and if you’re an adult who plays video games, it should really be a title you make time for.

In my review, I highlighted some of its many positive traits, but as you prepare to dive into its criminal delights over the weekend, one element I’d especially like to point out is its viability as a game to play with your partner. Like an excellent prestige TV crime show, GTAVI is a game that features a rich, dramatic, funny, and well-written story that I genuinely believe has the potential to be a good time for both a player and a viewer, though, admittedly, the person who gets to enjoy running the sticks is probably having the most fun.

However you plan to enjoy it, here’s hoping Grand Theft Auto VI turns out to be worth the wait you’ve likely had for it. For my part, it certainly has been, and I suspect you’ll find it only gets better the deeper into the game you go.

The running joke publisher Devolver Digital has made with this “spectacular remaster of the original remake of the unreleased action-platformer starring the most famous video game mascot of all time” is that it launched the same day as Grand Theft Auto VI. Volvy’s Adventure has been positioned as a tongue-in-cheek competitor to Rockstar’s behemoth, with Devovler even releasing a trailer that is a shot-for-shot parody of GTA VI’s. While I’ve chuckled at these stunts, Volvy’s Adventure isn’t just a joke game. It’s actually pretty fun.

For one, it’s developed by a respectable studio in Doinksoft, the team behind fun indie games like Gato Roboto, Gunbrella, and this year’s Dark Scrolls. Vovly’s Adventure is a 16-bit 2D platformer where players use Volvy’s oversized fist to punch through objects, which, in turn, propels him in the same direction. Thus, platforming is a fast-paced and explosive exercise in soaring fist-first through barriers and enemies, collecting items, and burrowing through certain platforms. The platforming feels pretty good, and it’s backed by a catchy soundtrack; the destruction is satisfying; and the levels are relatively brief, making it easy to plow through.

I wasn’t sure what to expect from Volvy’s Adventure beyond the marketing jokes, but it’s got some sauce. Sitting at the budget price of $5 (and a launch discount of $3.74), it’s a curiosity that’s easy to check out.

Australia Did It, from Rami Ismail and his team at Aesthetician Labs, hit a little snag with its publicized release date. Valve got backed up approving the release of games on its platform and a handful of games were affected. Australia Did It, despite the unexpected delay, is out... and it's good! Here's what Brian Shea wrote in his review: "Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world."

God of War Sons of Sparta is... underwhelming, to be blunt. You can read my review here. The game is a prequel where you play as a young Kratos and go on a 2D Metroid-inspired adventure with your brother, Deimos. If you are interested in getting the full God of War story, there are some interesting narrative and character details in the game, but it has some shortcomings. What's surprising about its re-release this week is that it is now available on PS4. An unexpected "new" platform to say the least.

#4068. Where To Find Vespucci Island In GTA 6

Vespucci Island in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a great place to find some high-value cars, weapons, and sellable goods.

Grand Theft Auto 6's map is massive, so it's no surprise that players are finding themselves lost from time to time. Eventually, many will likely come to know Leonida's roads as well as those in their real-life hometowns, but for now we thankfully have guides like this and in-game GPS.

Vespucci Island is one of the many islands in Leonida, and while knowing its name could be enough to locate it on the map, it's still hard to find a small location if you don't know where to start looking. So, if you're looking for Vespucci Island because you heard about some Easter egg or car there, keep reading to find out just where to find it.

Vespucci Island is one of the three Rialto Islands in Vice-Dale County. The Rialto Islands are the islands along one of the bridges from Vice City to Vice Beach, and Vespucci Island is the middle one with a large oval shape. If you zoom in on this area, you should see it clearly labeled, or at least see a faint outline since you haven't discovered it yet.

Mark this part of the map with a destination point, then use your GPS to drive out to it and register the island on your map. Vespucci Island is pretty small, so there's not a ton to see there, but a few points of interest include:

Vespucci Island is full of mansions and nice cars, but that also means a lot of security systems, alarms, and cars with trackers. So be careful and remember to scan vehicles before breaking in.

#4067. Quantic Dream addresses toxicity, tech bugs and tutorials for Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta 2 - here's how to get a key

Here are the start and end times for the second Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta, as well as what's new in this latest test.

Quantic Dream has opened up its upcoming fantasy MOBA for a second closed beta weekend starting from today, January 29, until 9AM UTC on Monday February 2.

The closed beta is for PC only in Europe, Asia and North America and potential players can register to join the waitlist for a key at the game’s official website or on the Spellcasters Chronicles Steam page. Players who had access to the first closed beta will automatically have access to the second, but you can sign up on both the site and Steam to increase your chances of entry.

The MOBA genre is competitive in every sense and Quantic Dream is trying to break into it with a Magic the Gathering-esque spin on the format. Players build a deck of cards before queuing into teams of 3, then face off as battling mages, summoning creatures, building fortifications and casting spells rather than choosing a Hero with unique abilities in the traditional MOBA style.

Beta content includes a new map, 6 new spells and 5 new summon creatures for your deck, as well as 3 new buildings too.

Also new for this second closed beta is an introduction and tutorial for some of the game’s finer details, as well as a text chat for strategising and much-needed player reporting system to go with it. It will also feature early versions of the Spellcaster customisation system and ranked matches.

Quantic Dream has said that this closed beta places a strong emphasis on performance, memory usage and overall gameplay stability to create a smoother experience, so with that in mind, here are the minimum and recommended PC specs:

Spellcasters Chronicles is the first ever multiplayer online game from Quantic Dream, the French studio best known for cinematic narrative games like Detroit: Become Human, Heavy Rain and Beyond: Two Souls.

A TV adaptation of the latter game is reportedly in development, or the rights for one have been acquired at least. Elsewhere, Quantic Dream’s long-rumoured game in the Star Wars franchise was revealed as Star Wars Eclipse, a return-to-type narrative action game set in the High Republic era of a galaxy far, far away.

#4066. Opinion: After Finishing Ocarina Of Time, I'm Left Jonesing For A Proper Sequel

Yesterday I finished the Ocarina of Time remake. Having replayed the original over the summer with my kids, we've beansed it through this one, taking our time to enjoy the view and appreciate the myriad changes, but already knowing exactly where to go and what to do.

What is there left to say about it? It's an excellent video game, a thoroughly impressive revamp which changes enough to feel modern without trampling over the original. I have a handful of tiny issues with it (the Sheik reveal always felt a bit obvious, but here I don't see how anybody won't see it coming), but they're minuscule in the scheme of things. Childhoods haven't been ruined, and at a time when genuine warm fuzzies are in short supply, Nintendo has delivered.

Still, after catching the Loach and using the in-game menus to track down the last Skulltulas and Heart Pieces — and even dipping into Zelda Notes and OCD-ing every last rupee-filled Treasure Chest for the magic 100% rating in the app — I was left feeling a tad...deflated? That's not quite the word, but there was an emptiness.

It's a stunning game and I enjoyed every second, but as a remake it naturally lacked the same sense of wonder you get from exploring and not knowing what's around the next corner. Delight up the wazoo, but not so much in the 'surprise' department.

The natural conclusion, given the very warm reception and impressive sales, is that Nintendo will crack straight on with Majora's Mask next. And yes, absolutely; MM is my personal favourite, so of course I'll take a remake. It's the least-brainer-y no-brainer since Ocarina 3D was a hit.

However, already knowing the world and the story does take something away from the Zelda experience, and having now appreciated this remake's gorgeous art style, the presentation would provide less novelty next time, too.

"It's not as exciting when you know what's coming," said my seven-year-old last night after we rolled credits. Both kids still sat beside me for "30 hours or more" over the past three weeks, mind, so let's not blow this out of proportion. I could feel her attention wandering at times, though, even with the grandeur of the visuals and all the additions.

So, I've now got a dilemma. Do I show them the original Majora's Mask as planned, or wait for the hypothetical remake and preserve its narrative twists and turns? Would they prefer to be surprised? Despite wanting to see the Zora mask in action, they'd both rather wait. Saying they'll be old enough to control it themselves in a couple of years may have soured them on watching me play the "square-y" version now. Fingers crossed Nintendo actually makes the thing.

The parent's perspective isn't a consideration for everyone, it's just an interesting conundrum. I'm also aware that none of this is an issue for Ocarina newbies! For me personally, though, as much as I would/will devour Majora's Mask, there's another approach that could bring the best of both worlds. A link, ahem, between worlds, if you will. What about a brand new sequel to Ocarina?

Imagine a game which continues the Hero of Time's journey, with Link grown up — in his mid-20s, say — exploring a Hyrule changed by his heroics in the first game. This Link saved Hyrule and Termina, and (almost) nobody in his world knows it. That's fertile ground for a story only hinted at in Twilight Princess.

The Ocarina remake gives glimpses of a larger world beyond Hyrule's hills. How about a sequel that lets us explore those, expanding the horizons and pushing out the frontiers of this contained kingdom? A game which taps our emotional connections and nostalgia but brings something truly unknown as well.

Could that be it? Could that integration of old and new — Ocarina + BOTW — be a direction for the series as a whole? Mashing two known ideas to make something notionally fresh is fandom 101, of course. "What if Ocarina but bigger?" "What if old Link travelled back with a warning!" "What if Dark Link was a premonition and the Hero of Time has to save Hyrule from his own ego!" It's easy to pump out the 'what ifs'.

It's also easy to say, "Oh, just put old-school Ocarina-like dungeons into the open world!" It's a design headache, to be sure, but also a problem Nintendo has the know-how to tackle.

I just feel like there's more gold to mine from this world and this engine beyond a straightforward Majora's Mask remake. I'd play that and love it, the same as if they announced A Link to the Past or a reimagined version of the NES original. But I have played those games already - a vital element of the Zelda formula is missing in any remake.

Not feeling like a 'stopgap' project to train up staff while Aonuma and co. work out how the hell to follow up Tears of the Kingdom is one of this remake's most impressive qualities. We've already asked the question about whether that open-world Hyrule could withstand a third entry, and a direct sequel to TOTK seems unlikely. In some ways, remaking The Best Game of All Time was a mighty clever distraction.

However, if Nintendo doesn't have some revolutionary new take on Zelda up its sleeve just yet, I'd love to see them exploit this Hyrule and explore this Link's story some more. The last time they told a new story with a Link from long ago, we got the sublime A Link Between Worlds. Yes. Yes, please.

Let us know below how you'd feel about more adventures in strange new (and old) worlds with the Hero of Time, whether that's revisiting Termina or something else entirely.

#4065. Grand Theft Auto VI Shatters Records, Making $3.79 Billion In 24 Hours As The Biggest Entertainment Launch Ever

Grand Theft Auto VI dropped yesterday to massive success, and while we expected it to do well, hearing the numbers behind the historic launch day is still staggering. According to a statement obtained by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier and IGN, Rockstar has confirmed that the open-world juggernaut made $3.79 billion in 24 hours. This makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time – it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and it's not especially close.

Schreier goes on to confirm that much of that money comes from GTA VI's record-breaking pre-orders. It turns out, there were 32.5 million pre-sales, which is a truly mind-bending number. For context, its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, currently the second best-selling game of all time, sold 11.21 million copies in the first 24 hours – GTAVI nearly triples that figure. In pre-orders alone, the game has become the 30th best-selling game of all time, with more copies sold in the first day than Elden Ring and Super Mario Odyssey have sold, period.

In terms of the dollar amount, GTAVI's $3.79 billion in 24 hours is not just more money than any film has made in its opening weekend; it's more money than any movie has ever made in the box office – even Avengers: Endgame, which currently holds the highest worldwide gross, is still shy of $3 billion after several successful theatrical runs.

Grand Theft Auto VI also set the record on Metacritic for the highest-reviewed game of all time (with an average critic score of 99), and it headlined this week's rollout of the Game Awards 2026 nominees, with more nominations than any other game. We also loved it, and our editor-in-chief Matt Miller scored it a perfect 10.

#4064. Infinity Nikki ushers in the Year of the Horse with... a deer-themed Version 2.2

Chromatic Beings Everbright, the latest major Infinity Nikki update, has arrived, bringing Chinese New Year celebrations vibe to the game.

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other big addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

As with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

#4063. GTA 6 Glitch Unlocks The FPS On Xbox Series X|S, But With Multiple Drawbacks

It's a bug related to Quick Resume on Series X|S

Update [Mon 23rd Nov 2026, 6:52pm]: The folks over at Digital Foundry have also now taken a look at this, concluding that the unlocked FPS is still too inconsistent to make an official version viable as things stand.

Their analysis is pretty fascinating though, and you can watch it up above.

News Digital Foundry Analyses Whether GTA 6 Could Benefit From 40FPS On Xbox Series X

"A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense"

Original Story: If there's anything we could add to GTA 6 as things stand, it'd be an official 60FPS mode. That's obviously not possible right now due to how demanding the game is on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S hardware, even in the case of the PS5 Pro.

Interestingly though, over the weekend, players have discovered the ability to activate what some are calling a "60FPS Glitch" or "60FPS Bug" on Xbox consoles, forcing the game to unlock its FPS and run at a higher frame rate than it's actually supposed to.

Someone called Meowwie64 on Reddit appears to have found this, and here's what they did to activate it:

Now, as mentioned, there are multiple drawbacks here. The first one is that the glitch speeds up most aspects of the game, making it run faster than intended (and look like it's in fast-forward mode!). This is obviously not an ideal way to enjoy GTA 6, and serves as an immediate deal-breaker in my view.

Another one is that reaching 60FPS is pretty much impossible under normal gameplay circumstances. If you're driving down a highway, for example, you're likely only going to get around 35-40FPS at max, with 60FPS and above being saved for situations that require no graphical intensity whatsoever.

And finally, it should be noted that GTA 6 was never intended to be run this way on Xbox Series X|S, and therefore you could run into all sorts of issues - crashes, bugs, maybe even your console overheating. That last one is unlikely, but the game has been specifically built to run at 30FPS on these machines, so it's not worth pushing it in our view.

We'll leave you with some footage of this glitch running on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S down below (courtesy of the always-excellent Fuzion Xbox Testing), and prepare for it to be officially fixed in an upcoming GTA 6 update.

#4061. Zenelss Zone Zero Version 2.6 has you playing as an event planner and social media manager for an idol group

Zenelss Zone Zero's Encore for an Old Dream has a good excuse for introducing some new mechanics to the action game.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming update, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for New Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

As always, there’s no reason not to catch up on the latest set of Zenless Zone Zero codes for some free in-game items.

#4060. Deborah Ann Woll Will Reprise Her Role As Laufey In Amazon's God Of War Series

Deborah Ann Woll, likely best known as Karen Page in Daredevil and Daredevil: Born Again, has just been cast as Laufey in the upcoming live-action God of War series. It's a perfect fit, not just because she's a great actress – Woll already portrays the character in the video games.

The live-action God of War series is currently in production, and after a series of headlines about Kratos, it's refreshing to get some news about his late wife, Faye. Also known as Laufey, she dies right before 2018's God of War (which the show is based on) begins. The game centers on a journey between Kratos and his son to spread Faye's ashes from the highest peak in the realms.

Faye is not present in 2018's God of War, but she appears in God of War Ragnarök in flashback and dream sequences. In this game, she's played by Deborah Ann Woll, an oddly high-profile casting for a relatively minor character. It all made sense earlier this year, however, when we learned Woll will reprise her role as the star of God of War Laufey, which tells Faye's story as she fights through a mythological underworld.

It's a cool piece of news, and it implies that Faye will have more of a presence in the series than in the first game, where she never appears at all. As for what shape that presence takes, we have no idea.

Woll joins the likes of Alastair Duncan, who plays Mimir and will also reprise his role. The two don't really interact in the games, however, so it's unlikely to see them share the screen in the series.

The main news around Prime Video's God of War is about its protagonist. Originally announced as Ryan Hurst, the actor suffered a serious injury on the set of the show and was replaced by Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy, Glass Onion) in August. Other key cast members include Callum Vinson as Atreus, Sonya Walger as Freya, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, and Ed Skrein as Baldur.

For more God of War, you can look forward to Woll's portrayal of Faye in God of War Laufey, though it recently got delayed.

#4059. GTA 6 Is 'Probably the Greatest Artistic Achievement in History', Says Cyberpunk 2 Director

Just about every veteran developer in the industry has been heaping praise on GTA 6 since its release last week, but I'm not sure any of that rampant positivity matches the thoughts of Igor Sarzynski.

Sarzynski is currently the creative director on Cyberpunk 2 (as it's officially known right now), having previously worked on both The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 — two games that are widely considered to be amongst the best that the open world genre has to offer.

In other words, Sarzynski knows what he's talking about when he says GTA 6 is "probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history". Now that's praise.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he noted on social media.

"Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle."

"Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled," Sarzynski jokes, suggesting that no one's going to match Rockstar's effort for quite some time. "I'mma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now."

GTAVI-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, i mean it. scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. cyberpunk 2 is cancelled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.

If you've played GTA 6, you can surely understand why every non-Rockstar developer is looking at it and being left in a state of near disbelief. We're not getting another release like it for years and years to come — and just like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, it's going to become the benchmark for open world games.

Still, there'll come a time when Cyberpunk 2 takes all the headlines — it's just that right now, it's hard to see beyond GTA 6 because it's absolutely bloody everywhere (and with good reason).

"Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavour," Sarzynski continues in a follow-up post.

"GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed," he concludes — and that's pretty much a perfect way to put it.

Do you agree with Sarzynski? Just how big of an achievement do you think GTA 6 really is? Have your mind blown in the comments section below.

@Fiendish-Beaver I don’t disagree with your statement in many ways.

However, on the subject of CDPR, with Cyberpunk 2077, every AAA and some even AA studios could absolutely deliver what they have.

They started “work” on Cyberpunk 2077 as far back as 2010-2011 if memory serves.

It was then in and out of development, until about 2016 when it was an all hands on deck approach. Not the start of development, simply at that point many more in the studio working on actively producing a working title.

Then, release came, again, I believe was around 2020. So say at that point 9-10 years of development, with 4 or just under/over years of true entire studio development of some sort.

Yet, they released a game so bad in its basic coding and functionality, that they claimed they weren’t aware of, to then claim they were aware of, then had journalists embargo to not tell of this until launch/very close to launch.

They then offered mass refunds, one of the industries first physical and digital refunds of its kind. Where even I sent them my disc back to their office directly and got a refund.

It then took them up until shall we say about now, maybe being generous a year or so ago to get the game to where most were led to believe it should be and would have been at release.

CDPR conned the public, for financial gain, knowingly, and they squandered hundreds of thousands and likely millions actually on course correcting.

When all they had to do was not release the game until it was finished.

So whilst from what I witness every day in the industry I agree with your points as a whole, we shouldn’t give credit to what CDPR could do with a billion dollars, when the best example of what they did with less was verging on fraudulently selling and advertising a product, pulling it from sale, taking years to “fix” it and then regain consumer confidence.

Many may have forgiven and/or forgotten. They shouldn’t, and I sure won’t.

CDPR have a wonderful vision in their artistry, and I hope they go on to have success upon success. But what R* have achieved is miles beyond what many could achieve even with the money.

There’s numerous engines I’ve used over the years, entire workflows that quite literally can’t physically do what R* have pulled off with their team and technology. It needs really making clear to the laypeople of the world that this isn’t simply more money and talent, this is entirely new ways of approaching how to develop a game and how to use the the resources available.

CDPR literally looked at what they had, made mockups of ideas that were conceptual at best and ran with selling concept art that in some cases they still haven’t accomplished.

I don’t even have a history of playing a lot of R* content. But they have achieved something that money can’t currently buy. That’s the impressive part.

However, as stated, completely agree and disagree but not entirely. 😂 Peace and love on earth etc.

As without it I can’t excuse spending 6 months on a global sabbatical just meandering through the technology and discovering things on a whim.

It’s an odd industry really, it’s a lot like being a pop star, you’re told what to create, the timeline for when it’s expected to be completed, told how much will be charged for it, where and when it will be sold.

My happiness with the art I create matters only to the person viewing, yet the person that decides everything I create cares not for my happiness with it.

Problem is, I was forever going back through them and altering elements, and instead of shortening them, they would end up longer still, and I was always tinkering with them.

I often think about revisiting them as I never tried to get them published, but things changed for me when I met my second (now sadly deceased) wife. When I met her I dropped my writing, and even after her passing, I never returned to it, and instead fell headlong into gaming, and now I just cannot imagine spending long hours writing instead of gaming. Don't misunderstand me, I loved writing, and the writing process, but I think I probably enjoy gaming more, and so I'm not sure I'll return to it, but never say never, I guess...

@dark_knightmare2 It's a real shame that you're taking a celebration of what most believe is a landmark achievement in gaming and finding some way to be miserable about it. You're the guy at a baby shower talking about how the cake sucks.

@Fiendish-Beaver I am tremendously sorry to hear of the passing of your late wife that you experienced. Experiencing a great deal of loss myself, I know how much isn’t described by simply stating they are lost.

They’re there, in reverberations and memories at the very least, but grieving is a process I don’t believe fully ends, you sort of just learn to see things through another lens. Sometimes that is rose tinted and sometimes it’s darkness, but it’s always possible to see through them in time.

I won’t for a second try to tell you what to do, but maybe in time try to compel yourself to finish the writing, not in spite of all you experienced and how it changed you, but to have something you experienced change the way you write subconsciously and have it remembered forever.

When I lost my parents, I thought I’d change my career, I couldn’t create because all I could think of was the sheer volume of loss. How does one go about adding to the world when so focused on what has been taken from it.

Yet I found a way, I somehow found a way to regain a confidence not in myself, but in wanting to allow the light to win, and allow the work to speak of something I might not fully understand, but hopefully marks a time for someone out there that can gain from it.

Either way, you’re a creative with a story to tell. I for one would very much like to purchase anything literary you create no doubt.

Just remember, art knows no time, it’s there waiting for you if you ever find a moment.

I once tried to write a book on my dad’s typewriter, but then quickly learned it’s a very vulnerable process. Hence, I stopped, as vulnerability after a loss is never something one yearns for.

I think you will publish one day, the time will present itself, when it does, let me know. Who knows, it could help to heal another not just yourself.

In the meantime, gaming being your escapism only adds strings to your subconscious bow. If you ever need to scream or almost silently whisper, creative to creative, and grief exposed to another, you know where I am.

#4058. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4057. "We Cannot Believe We Are Reaching Milestones Like This" - Queen's Domain Dev Celebrates Opening Sales

The FromSoft-inspired RPG Queen's Domain might have launched in one of the busiest periods of game releases in recent memory, but that's not to say nobody has been picking it up.

Indeed, the game has got off to a rather strong sales start, with developer Freshly Baked and publisher Future Friends confirming that the devilishly difficult indie has already surpassed 300,000 sales across all platforms.

"We cannot believe we are reaching milestones like this," the dev shared in a celebratory post on Bluesky. "Thank you to everyone who has played, enjoyed and shared their Queen’s Domain journey".

⭐ 300K COPIES SOLD! ⭐ We cannot believe we are reaching milestones like this! Thank you to everyone who has played, enjoyed and shared their Queen’s Domain journey 🖤

The media landscape has been particularly preoccupied with the likes of Ocarina of Time and GTA 6 throughout November, but it seems that almost everyone who has played this one has fallen in love with its throwback visuals and classic King's Field vibes.

We're certainly big fans of it here at Nintendo Life, calling it "one of the best surprises of the year" in our 9/10 review. Here's hoping that its audience continues to grow in its second month on sale.

#4055. One Of Our Favorite Action Games From Gamescom, Showa American Story, Has Been Delayed To 2027

Showa American Story is set in a world where Japan's 1980s economic prowess was strong enough to purchase America, and so it did. Taking place in Neo Yokohama, formerly Hollywood, this raunchy, zany action game was one of our favorites at Gamescom 2026, but unfortunately, we'll have to wait a little longer than expected to experience more of this adventure.

That's because developer Nekcom Entertainment and publisher 4Divinity have revealed that Showa American Story has been delayed to next year. Originally due out sometime this year (though it became clear that wasn't going to happen given the radio silence as we near the year's end), Showa American Story will now launch on PlayStation 5 and PC on October 28, 2027.

"Reaching this milestone after five years of development means a lot to our entire team," the studio writes in a statement. "With core game content now complete, we're dedicating our full focus to polishing and optimizing the experience so that when you step into Showa American Story, it feels cohesive, responsive, and complete. Thank you for your continued support, enthusiasm, and patience along the way. We can't wait to welcome you on October 28, 2027."

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Showa American Story hands-on preview from this year's Gamescom. After that, check out our list of the top 10 action games to play right now.

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

#4052. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4051. God of War Laufey Star Will Reprise Role for Live-Action TV Show

God of War Laufey’s lead Deborah Ann Woll will reprise her role as Kratos’ wife Faye in Amazon Prime’s upcoming live-action TV adaptation.

The actress – who also played the character in God of War Ragnarok – will star opposite Dave Bautista’s Kratos in the glitzy show.

The re-telling should end up feeling quite familiar, as Alastair Duncan will also return as Mimir.

Fans of the franchise will know Woll dies at the start of the story, kickstarting Kratos’ quest as he and son Atreus embark on a journey to scatter her ashes.

But we now know, during that period, Faye is trapped in a kind of afterlife for the gods known as the Everywhen. That’s where God of War Laufey will take place.

It’ll be interesting to see whether the TV show pulls in elements from the upcoming PS5 game, or if Woll’s role here will be to show Kratos’ family life prior to the events of the main game.

There’s no release date for the show just yet, but filming restarted in October with Baustita in the lead role, after previous actor Ryan Hurst was recast due to sustaining an injury on set.

Woll is an accomplished actress and knows the character inside-out, so this casting makes perfect sense to me.

#4049. Grand Theft Auto VI Reaches Highest Concurrent Player Count Ever For PS5, More than 683 Million Hours Logged Already

Grand Theft Auto VI hasn't even been out for a week, and it's already broken so many records that it's hard to keep up. It made $3.79 billion in just 24 hours after its November 19 launch, making it the biggest entertainment launch of all time. It comes as no surprise, then, that Rockstar Games' latest crime saga is also shattering records specifically on PlayStation 5.

In a new PlayStation Blog post, the company has revealed that more than 39 million unique players have booted up GTA VI on PS5, with the game setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer games such as Helldivers II, free-to-play games like Fortnite, and single-player releases like Elden Ring. What's more, PS5 players have already logged a cumulative 683 million hours of GTA VI gameplay – that's nearly 78,000 years' worth of time.

Other records for GTA VI on PS5 include the game giving PlayStation the "largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays," and GTA VI being the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles since the game's launch.

This is likely only the beginning of records GTA VI will continue to break.

In the meantime, read Game Informer's GTA VI review to find out why it's one of the greatest games we've ever played, then read the game's first update patch notes to see what's changed. After that, read Game Informer's exclusive interview with Rockstar about the romance between Jason and Lucia, and then check out this feature on the 102 things we actually got before GTA VI. #4048. Heartopia shows off My Little Pony collaboration, and there's a pre-launch event to hold you over

Heartopia’s My Little Pony collaboration is close, and the pre-launch event has already kicked off.

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

If any of that sounds interesting, definitely log in now to play the pre-launch event, which should hold you over until the proper show kicks off Saturday. If you’re already enjoying Heartopia, you likely want to learn about Onsen Egg Promise locations, Fish locations, and Bug locations - all of which can be found at those links.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.
